- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.53) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (<0.3) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Avoid long-term over-optimism in 30-day forecasts — cap upward trend after 3–5 consecutive days of rising prices.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.18–0.53), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- Correct for “overshoot after spike” — if forecast peaks >10% above recent 7-day high, subtract 5–10% from peak.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.18–0.27 for 3+ days), forecast should trend downward — adjust downward slope by 1–2% per day.
- Don’t assume sentiment directly translates to price — if sentiment is high but price is flat, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
